title: Rational functions are the product of the generic local rings
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] whose underlying topological space has finitely many irreducible components $X_1,\dots,X_n$ [def-weil-irreducible-components], and let $\eta_i\in X_i$ be the generic point of $X_i$ [def-sc-generic-point], unique by [lem-sc-scheme-sober]. Then every dense open subset $U\subseteq X$ contains $\eta_1,\dots,\eta_n$, and the map $$R(X)\longrightarrow\mathcal O_{X,\eta_1}\times\cdots\times\mathcal O_{X,\eta_n},\qquad [(U,f)]\longmapsto(f_{\eta_1},\dots,f_{\eta_n}),$$ from the ring of rational functions [def-sc-rational-functions] to the product of the stalks of the structure sheaf [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], sending a class to the germs of a representative, is well defined and a ring isomorphism. If $X$ is integral [def-pc-integral-scheme], then $n=1$, $X_1=X$, and $R(X)\cong\mathcal O_{X,\eta}$ is a field.

source.place: Lemma 01RV (label lemma-integral-scheme-rational-functions, line 12705), first and third assertions; its last step cites Algebra Lemma 00EU (label lemma-minimal-prime-reduced-ring)

proof.text: Put V_i equal to the complement of the union of all components other than X_i. The components form a finite set because components is an equivalence from Fin n. The V_i are open, and Mathlib closure_sUnion_irreducibleComponents_sdiff_singleton gives closure(V_i) = X_i, hence V_i is contained in X_i and nonempty. The generic-point open-set criterion then gives eta_i in V_i. Distinct V_i are disjoint because V_i avoids X_j for j different from i. This uses the component cover and maximality via the cited Mathlib closure theorem [lem-sc-irreducible-components-cover, def-weil-irreducible-components, def-sc-generic-point].

source.place: Lemma 01RV (label lemma-integral-scheme-rational-functions, line 12705), proof, first sentence: the sets U_i = (U ∩ X_i) \ ∪_{j≠i} X_j

proof.text: Dense opens are the opens containing all generic points (first assertion; Stacks 01RV, proof, first sentence). Let $U$ be a dense open. The open set $V_i$ of step 1 is nonempty ($\eta_i\in V_i$), so the dense $U$ meets it, say in $y$; $y\in V_i\subseteq X_i$, so $U\cap X_i\neq\emptyset$ and hence $\eta_i\in U$ by step 1. So $\eta_1,\dots,\eta_n\in U$. Conversely, if an open $W$ contains $\eta_1,\dots,\eta_n$, its closure contains $\overline{\{\eta_i\}}=X_i$ for every $i$, hence contains $X_1\cup\dots\cup X_n=X$: $W$ is dense. In particular, if $W_i$ is an open with $\eta_i\in W_i\subseteq V_i$ for each $i$, then $W:=W_1\cup\dots\cup W_n$ is a dense open subset of $X$ and a disjoint union of the $W_i$ (Stacks: '$U_i$ is nonempty open as it contains $\eta_i$, contained in $X_i$, and $\bigcup U_i\subset U\subset X$ is dense').

source.place: Lemma 01RV (label lemma-integral-scheme-rational-functions, line 12705), proof, first sentence

proof.text: The map is a well defined ring homomorphism (Stacks 01RV, the string of equalities: $R(X)=\operatorname{colim}_{U\text{ dense}}\mathcal O_X(U)$, the second equality being the description of $R(X)$ by sections). By [def-sc-rational-functions] $R(X)=\varinjlim_U\mathcal O_X(U)$ over the dense opens $U$. For a dense open $U$ we have $\eta_i\in U$ by step 2, so the germ maps $\mathcal O_X(U)\to\mathcal O_{X,\eta_i}$, $f\mapsto f_{\eta_i}$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], are ring homomorphisms, and so is $\varphi_U:\mathcal O_X(U)\to\prod_i\mathcal O_{X,\eta_i}$, $f\mapsto(f_{\eta_i})_i$. They are compatible with restriction to a smaller dense open $W\subseteq U$: $(f|_W)_{\eta_i}=f_{\eta_i}$, since $\eta_i\in W$ and germs are unchanged by restriction to a neighbourhood. Hence (universal property of the colimit, or directly: if $(U,f)\sim(V,g)$ with $f|_W=g|_W$ on a dense open $W\subseteq U\cap V$, then $f_{\eta_i}=(f|_W)_{\eta_i}=(g|_W)_{\eta_i}=g_{\eta_i}$) they induce a well-defined ring homomorphism $\varphi:R(X)\to\prod_i\mathcal O_{X,\eta_i}$, $[(U,f)]\mapsto(f_{\eta_1},\dots,f_{\eta_n})$; sums and products are respected because they are computed on $U\cap V$ by restriction and germs are additive and multiplicative.

source.place: Lemma 01RV (label lemma-integral-scheme-rational-functions, line 12705), proof, first and second equalities of the displayed string

proof.text: Injectivity, following the third equality of Stacks 01RV. The dense-open diagram is filtered in the restriction direction, so every element of its ring colimit is represented by a section [def-sc-rational-functions]. For representatives s on U and t on T with equal generic germs, the stalk equality criterion [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] supplies neighborhoods W_i of eta_i contained in both U and T on which their restrictions agree. The union D of these neighborhoods is dense by step 2. Sheaf locality [def-pc-scheme] gives equality of the two restrictions on D, and the colimit relation gives equality of the represented rational functions. Disjointness of the W_i is unnecessary for this step.

source.place: Lemma 01RV (label lemma-integral-scheme-rational-functions, line 12705), proof, third equality of the displayed string

proof.text:
Surjectivity (Stacks 01RV, third to fifth equalities: the colimit of $\prod_i\mathcal O_X(U_i)$ over the tuples $(U_i)$ with $\eta_i\in U_i$ is $\prod_i\varinjlim_{U_i
i\eta_i}\mathcal O_X(U_i)=\prod_i\mathcal O_{X,\eta_i}$). Let $(s_1,\dots,s_n)\in\prod_i\mathcal O_{X,\eta_i}$. By [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] every element of a stalk is a germ: $s_i=(g_i)_{\eta_i}$ for some open $W_i
i\eta_i$ and $g_i\in\mathcal O_X(W_i)$; replacing $W_i$ by $W_i\cap V_i$ and $g_i$ by its restriction (same germ) we may assume $W_i\subseteq V_i$, so the $W_i$ are pairwise disjoint (step 1). On the open $W=W_1\sqcup\dots\sqcup W_n$ the sections $g_i$ agree on all overlaps $W_i\cap W_j=\emptyset$ ($i
eq j$), so by the gluing axiom of the sheaf $\mathcal O_X$ [def-pc-scheme] there is $g\in\mathcal O_X(W)$ with $g|_{W_i}=g_i$. $W$ is dense by step 2, so $[(W,g)]\in R(X)$ [def-sc-rational-functions], and $\varphi([(W,g)])=(g_{\eta_i})_i=((g|_{W_i})_{\eta_i})_i=(s_i)_i$. Hence $\varphi$ is surjective, and with steps 3 and 4 a ring isomorphism.

proof.text: Integral case, following the final sentence of Stacks 01RV. If X is integral [def-pc-integral-scheme], it is irreducible and its irreducible components form the singleton {X} [def-weil-irreducible-components]. Thus Fin n is nonempty and subsingleton, so n = 1, and each component is X. Evaluation of the product at any index is a ring equivalence, compatible with the germ equivalence of steps 3-5. The field clause of [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction] is available directly as Mathlib AlgebraicGeometry.isField_stalk_of_closure_mem_irreducibleComponents: reducedness and closure {eta_i} in irreducibleComponents X imply that its stalk is a field. Transport this property through the evaluation equivalence to the rational-function ring. The affine-fraction construction and the choice of an affine open need not be repeated here.

split_report.summary: Split following Stacks 01RV's proof exactly: the sets V_i = X minus the other components (Stacks' U_i) are open, contain eta_i, lie in X_i and are pairwise disjoint (needs X = union of components, Topology 004W, new Mathlib leaf lem-sc-irreducible-components-cover); a dense open meets each V_i hence contains each eta_i, and an open containing all eta_i is dense; the germ maps give a well-defined ring map on the colimit R(X); Stacks' equalities colim_{U dense} O(U) = colim prod O(U_i) = prod colim O(U_i) = prod O_{X,eta_i} are written out as injectivity (locality of the sheaf on the disjoint cover by W_i ⊆ V_i) and surjectivity (gluing germs on disjoint W_i ⊆ V_i). The integral case: X irreducible is its own only component, and O_{X,eta} is a field by the existing Mathlib leaf lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction (the 00EU step). Statement unchanged; stmt_deps unchanged. The reduced clause of 01RV (R(X) = prod kappa(eta_i)) is not in the statement and not proved.
